subject: Atlas Health — on-demand fallback & true-up terms
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood hosted pricing — initial commit + on-demand fallback options

Hi Lena,

Thanks again for the time today. As discussed, I attached a concise proposal that outlines a 12-month commit tier and the fallback on-demand rates we expect customers to rely on for burst traffic. A few quick notes up front:

- Proposed commit: $120k/month (equivalent to ~1.2B tokens/month at our standard generation mix)
- On-demand fallback rate (when commit exhausted): $0.16 per 1k tokens
- Burst buffer: ability to burst an extra 20% above commit at on-demand rates for up to 72 hours without immediate penalties; anything beyond triggers true-up reconciliation at month-end.

Two questions we had for you and procurement before we finalize:
1) Does Atlas require a minimum monthly invoice floor for the PO (we can set a $100k minimum if that helps with internal budgeting)?
2) Would Atlas prefer automatic true-up billing (we invoice the overage at the end of the month) or a manual approval flow for overages >$25k?

I've attached the proposal PDF and included a SOW draft for scope alignment. Rishi is looped in on pricing and Grace will handle contract terms and billing details.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Hosted_Proposal_Atlas_2026-05-20.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)]
[Attachment: SOW_Atlas_Redwood_2026-05-21.docx (DOCX, 3 pages)]

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlashealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosted pricing — initial commit + on-demand fallback options

Hi Naomi — thanks for the proposal and for the clear breakdown. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can commit to a 12-month agreement, but the initial budgeted monthly spend is $95k; is there flexibility to re-tier pricing at $95k?
- For bursts: 20% buffer sounds reasonable but can you confirm how that interacts with SLA/latency guarantees? We need burst requests to maintain the same p95 latency target.
- On true-up: Procurement prefers automatic true-up billing, but we need a notification window (48 hours) before any overage >$10k is applied so we can approve or pause traffic.

We will pull in procurement (procurement@atlashealth.com) for the PO once terms are locked. Also copying our platform lead if we need technical confirmation.

Regards,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform, Atlas Health

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood hosted pricing — initial commit + on-demand fallback options

Thanks Lena — very helpful. Answers inline and next steps below.

- Flex on commit tier: We can re-tier to a $95k monthly commit. That would move Atlas into our "Commit Tier B" with a committed-per-token discount of 18% off list (we've modeled that in the attached updated sheet).
- SLA during burst: Our serving runtime keeps the same routing and latency SLOs for short bursts. For >20% sustained burst beyond 72 hours we do a capacity reallocation which may affect p95 for peak windows; however we will guarantee p99 failover and provide credits if monthly p95 exceeds agreed SLO due to capacity routing (we can bake precise credit formula into the SLA).
- True-up workflow: We can do automatic true-up at month-end, but we'll implement a 48-hour pre-charge notification for overages exceeding $10k. That notification will include usage details and suggested throttles you can apply; you then have 48 hours to respond before the charge posts.

Next steps: I updated the proposal to reflect the $95k/month commit and adjusted on-demand fallback rate to $0.175 per 1k tokens (this is slightly higher than the larger commit band). Attached: revised proposal and a short sample billing flow diagram.

Would you and procurement be available Mon/Tue for a brief 30-min alignment to finalize notification wording and the PO floor?

Best,
Naomi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Hosted_Proposal_Atlas_2026-05-21-v2.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)]

From: procurement@atlashealth.com
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosted pricing — initial commit + on-demand fallback options

Hi Naomi / Rishi,

Procurement here. We reviewed the v2 proposal. A couple of items we need in the commercial terms before sending a PO:

- Minimum invoice floor: Atlas requires a $90k min monthly invoice floor for the first 90 days of the contract to align with our internal cost center allocations. Can Redwood accept a 90-day ramp floor of $90k, then revert to the $95k committed amount?
- Overage dispute window: we need a 21-day dispute window post-invoice for any billed overages (standard for us). Can you confirm?
- Pricing cap for bursts: prefer a cap so on-demand rates for bursts cannot exceed 2x the standard on-demand rate within the same billing month.

If you can confirm these items we can proceed with the PO. Also include the SOW page numbers that describe data handling and retention so Security can sign off.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Atlas Health
[procurement@atlashealth.com]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: procurement@atlashealth.com, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redwood hosted pricing — initial commit + on-demand fallback options

Hi Atlas procurement — appreciate the clarity. Responses below and proposed contract language we can include: 

1) 90-day ramp floor: Accepted. Contract clause: "For the first ninety (90) days following Effective Date, Customer agrees to a minimum invoice floor of $90,000 per month regardless of actual usage; thereafter the committed monthly amount will be $95,000."

2) Overage dispute window: We agree to a 21-day dispute window. Contract clause: "Customer may dispute billed overages within twenty-one (21) days of invoice receipt; undisputed amounts remain payable while disputed amounts are investigated."

3) Burst price cap: We accept a cap at 2x on-demand within the billing month. Contract clause: "On-demand burst pricing will not exceed 2x the prevailing on-demand rate in the same billing month; Redwood will apply the lower capped rate to all burst usage in that month. Exceptions for capacity emergencies will be documented and require mutual notification."

I'll have Grace add the clause text into the SOW and the commercial side of the Master Services Agreement. Naomi will route the updated doc for signature and DocuSign.

Thanks — Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Proposed_Contract_Clauses_Atlas_2026-05-22.txt (TXT, 1 page)]
